electrical-power-engineering.about: The Department of Electrical & Power Engineering is dedicated to education and research in power generation, transmission, electrical grids, energy auditing, and renewable energy integrations. Founded on the rich heritage of technical energy training in Bukhara, we collaborate with regional power grid administrations and industrial companies to train engineers who optimize and secure the national energy sector.

electrical-power-engineering.history:
The Department of Electrical and Power Engineering was established in 1977 under the name 'General Electrical Engineering', separated from the 'General Engineering Sciences' department under the leadership of M.T. Turdiev. Since 1978, evening classes in 'Electricity Supply for Industrial Enterprises, Cities and Agriculture' were offered, followed by daytime classes in 'Power Engineering' in 1985, and postgraduate programs in 2000.
The department was led by M.T. Turdiyev (1977-1985, 1994-2005), A.M. Abdullayev (1985-1994), N.N. Sadullayev (2005-2011), M.I. Maxmudov (2011-2018), and I.I. Xafizov (2018-2019).
In 2019, three separate departments were created: 'Electrical Mechanics and Technologies' (led by Assoc. Prof. I.I. Xafizov), 'Power Engineering' (led by Assoc. Prof. R.B. Jalilov), and 'Energy Audit' (led by M.I. Mahmudov).
Following structural reforms in the 2024-2025 academic year, these three departments were merged into the single 'Department of Electrical and Power Engineering'. N.N. Mirzayev served as head in 2024-2025, and Assoc. Prof. Latipov Saidmurod Tuyg'unovich has been leading it since the start of the 2025-2026 academic year.

In 2013, under Presidential Decree PQ-1954, it was renamed 'Information-Communication Systems of Technological Processes Control'. Today, it offers comprehensive Bachelor's and Master's degrees in automation, with evening and part-time education introduced in 2019.

information-and-communication-technologi.history: The department started its activity in 1979 under the name 'Applied Mathematics' at the Bukhara Food and Light Industry Technology Institute. Over the years, reflecting the growth and transformations of the industry, it was renamed 'Informatics' (1999), split into 'Informatics' and 'Modern Technologies of Teaching' (2001), recombined as 'Informatics and Information Technologies' (2005), renamed 'Information Technologies' (2015), and finally 'Information and Communication Technologies' (2017). The department has trained more than 3,000 specialists since 1996 and is equipped with modern computer laboratories and multimedia classrooms.

information-and-communication-technologi.research: The department actively conducts research in the areas of digital education methodology, machine learning, cybersecurity, IoT, and numerical modeling of turbulent jet flow of reacting gases. It participates in a key national research grant under the Committee for Sanitary-Epidemiological Peace and Public Health titled 'Information System for Vaccine Logistics Management'. Faculty members regularly present at international conferences and have published more than 30 papers in local and international journals.

economics-and-management.history: The history of economics education at the institute dates back to 1969, when the 'Economics' department was first established at the general technical faculty of the Tashkent Polytechnic Institute. In 1978, it was reorganized as the 'Political Economy' department at the Bukhara Food and Light Industry Technology Institute. In 1993, the 'Economics, Production Organization and Planning' department was split to form the 'Production and Management' department. Over the years, the departments evolved and split into 'Economics' and 'Management'. In 2024, they were merged once again to form the unified 'Economics and Management' department.
